title: Senior's toolkit: the core loop
summary: The init, plan, apply, show, output, graph, console, fmt and validate flags people who live in Terraform type every day.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the core loop
steps.body: These are the commands and flags an experienced Terraform engineer reaches for without looking them up. `alias tf=terraform` is set on this machine, as on most of theirs.

toolkit.what: Prepare a working folder: providers, modules, backend. Safe to run any time.
flags: pick the newest versions the constraints allow, and rewrite the lock file
fill in backend settings per environment
forget the old backend settings (no migration)
copy the state to a new backend
fail instead of changing the lock file (CI)

toolkit.what: Show what would change. Reads only.
flags: save it, to apply exactly this later
wait for a lock instead of failing at once

toolkit.what: Make the changes. With a saved plan it applies exactly that plan.
flags: apply the saved plan (no question asked)
skip the yes prompt (only with care)

toolkit.what: Print a saved plan or the current state, as text or JSON.
flags: machine-readable, for jq, policy tools and CI
plain text for logs and PR comments
toolkit.example: terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("delete")) | .address'

toolkit.what: Read the root module's outputs from the state.
flags: just the value, no quotes: for scripts
every output as JSON (sensitive ones included!)

toolkit.what: A REPL to try expressions and functions against the real configuration and state.
flags: with the same inputs as a plan

toolkit.what: The dependency graph in DOT (`dependent -> dependency`).
flags: the order a destroy would use

toolkit.what: Rewrite files in the canonical style. CI runs the check form.
flags: exit 3 if anything would change, write nothing

toolkit.what: Check syntax, references and types without touching any API (needs init).
flags: diagnostics for editors and CI annotations

steps.prompt: Match each flag to what it is for.
pairs: move to newer allowed provider versions
fail CI when files are not formatted
a bare value for a shell script
validate without access to the state

steps.prompt: What does this print? (`terraform console` evaluates expressions; try it on the machine in the next lesson.)
steps.explain: `cidrsubnet(prefix, newbits, netnum)` adds 8 bits to the /16 (giving /24 networks) and picks number 3. Planning subnets with it keeps the maths in code instead of a spreadsheet.

steps.prompt: CI must fail a pull request that changes the provider versions without saying so. Which `init` flag does that?
steps.explain: With `-lockfile=readonly`, `init` uses the committed lock file and fails if it would have to change it. Upgrades then happen only in a pull request where someone ran `init -upgrade` on purpose and committed the new lock file.

steps.prompt: The pipeline's first three lines. Fill the gaps.
steps.explain: Check formatting first (cheap, fails fast), install exactly the locked versions, then plan and keep the plan file. With `-detailed-exitcode` the job can skip the apply stage when nothing changed.
